title: WALMART SWATTING CALLS
full_story:
Effingham City Police are investigating a “swatting” call at the Effingham Walmart.  Several Walmart stores are reporting similar incidents in the region.

Just after 9 pm Monday, the Effingham Police Department responded to a reported threat at the Effingham Walmart.  An unknown male called the store and threatened to come to the location armed with a firearm and shoot individuals.

Officers arrived within minutes, secured the scene, and initiated a thorough search of the building and surrounding area.  Out of an abundance of caution and in the interest of public safety,

Walmart management elected to close the store for the remainder of the evening, while officers assisted with the orderly evacuation of employees and customers.

While conducting the initial investigation into the threat, officers determined this was a “swatting” call.  “Swatting” is “to make a false report of an ongoing serious crime in order to elicit a response from law enforcement.”  Further information revealed that other Walmarts in Illinois and Kentucky have had similar incidents in the past month.

Effingham Police Department Investigations Lieutenant Aaron Lange underscored the serious nature of these incidents, stating, “A false report of an active threat is not a prank, it is a serious criminal offense.  These intentional hoaxes create high-risk situations for responding officers, innocent victims, and the public, and they can have life-altering, or even deadly, consequences.  We will use every investigative tool available, including our local and state partners, to identify the individual or individuals responsible, and we will work with prosecutors to pursue the maximum penalties allowed under the law.  Anyone considering this type of hoax should understand that the consequences are severe, and they will be held accountable.”

title: CELL PHONE BAN
full_story:
Illinois Governor JB Pritzker signed the bell-to-bell cell phone ban legislation on Tuesday morning.

So as Illinois students return to school this fall, school boards and families will begin discussing and implementing a bell-to-bell cell phone ban, stemming from a new law that provides few exceptions for phone use during a school day.

Specifics of how bans will be enforced are left up to local school boards, which now have a full school year until they must adopt a policy that fits within the law’s minimum requirements.  It also doesn’t specifically provide school districts with funding to implement the ban, which has been common in other states.

Exceptions were made within the law for high school students that are enrolled in dual credit or other off campus programs and allows districts to choose if high school students can also use cell phones during passing periods and lunch.  Students with an IEP and other specific needs may also be granted an exception, according to the law.

title: RICHLAND FARM GRANT
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Agriculture is giving out almost $4 million to support local food producers.  And, a Richland County farm is getting a share.

Abundant Pastures in Claremont was awarded $38,182.27 and says they will use the money to purchase a refrigerated truck.  Abundant Pastures is a small family farm that strives to make high quality farm products available to as many people as possible.

The Local Food Infrastructure Grant Program was created to strengthen the capacity of Illinois producers and food businesses to store, process, package, aggregate, and distribute locally grown products.  Funding supports essential investments that help move Illinois-grown food from farm to consumer while building long term resilience within the state’s food supply chain.

The FY26 budget allocated funds for both collaborative and individual projects.  Selected grantees represent a diverse group of farms, cooperatives, nonprofits, food hubs, local governments, and food businesses, with awards ranging from $1,000–$250,000 for collaborative projects and $1,000–$75,000 for individual applicants.

“The Local Food Infrastructure Grant reflects our commitment to supporting Illinois agriculture,” said Illinois Department of Agriculture Director Jerry Costello II.  “These awards will help farmers, food businesses, and community partners expand their capacity and reach new markets.  When we invest in local food infrastructure, we are creating economic opportunity for businesses while ensuring Illinois residents have greater access to fresh, locally grown foods.”

Eligible applicants were required to meet administrative program rules, including Illinois entity with fewer than 50 employees involved in the production, processing, or distribution of value added agricultural products.  This year’s awardees will utilize grant funding to invest in critical infrastructure such as cold storage, processing equipment, transportation, aggregation facilities, and other improvements necessary to scale operations and improve local food access.

For more information about the Local Food Infrastructure Grant Program, including future funding opportunities, visit the Illinois Department of Agriculture’s website.

title: SOS AT STATE FAIR
full_story:
Illinois Secretary of State Alexi Giannoulias is inviting Illinois State Fair visitors to stop by the office’s tent to apply for a REAL ID, renew a driver’s license or vehicle registration, explore family history through free genealogy searches, meet award-winning Illinois authors and enjoy free activities for kids.

“The Illinois State Fair is all about celebrating what makes our state special and we’re excited to bring Secretary of State services directly to thousands of Illinoisans while they’re already enjoying a great family tradition,” Giannoulias said.  “Instead of making a separate trip to the DMV, fairgoers can take care of essential business, research their family history or spend time with their kids at an author reading.”

Families can enjoy Pop-a-Shot basketball hoops, a coloring station and appearances by Illinois authors, who will read their books aloud and sign copies during select times throughout the fair.  One hundred books from each author will be given away during scheduled appearances.  Featured writers include Gene Ha, Jeffrey Brown, Kate Hannigan, Betsy Bird and many others.

Fairgoers can also check out the office’s One-Stop-Shop experience, allowing customers to obtain both driver and vehicle services from a single counter.

To save time, visitors are encouraged to check www.ilsos.gov before coming to the fair to ensure they bring the required documents for their transaction.

Representatives from the Secretary of State’s Archives Department will conduct genealogy searches at no charge.  Representatives from the Business Services Department will be on hand to assist those wanting to start a business, file paperwork or look up an existing business.

The Secretary of State’s tent, located on Brian Raney Avenue near the southeast corner of the fairgrounds, will be open daily August 13th to 23rd from 10 am to 8 pm.  The tent will close at 4 pm on the final day of the fair.

title: LAKE LAND WELCOME WEEK
full_story:
Lake Land College will celebrate the start of the new school year by hosting Welcome Week, an event designed to help new and returning students settle into life at Lake Land and prepare for a successful year.

Welcome Week will begin the week before classes start and continue into the first week of the Fall semester, with activities and events offered Tuesday, August 18th through Saturday, August 22nd and Monday, August 24th through Thursday, August 27th.

Welcome Week will include a combination of fun and informative activities, including campus tours, information tables, games, giveaways and food trucks.  The activities are designed to help students settle in to life at Lake Land as they meet with staff and faculty, make new friends, discover helpful resources, pick up their textbooks and familiarize themselves with campus.

The activities will conclude on Wednesday, August 26th, with a campus-wide celebration known as Welcome Day.  Organized by the Lake Land College Student Activity Board, Welcome Day will be hosted in the College’s Field House and will include free lunch, games, giveaways and a wide range of information on student clubs and other opportunities for campus involvement.

For students taking classes in Effingham, an exclusive Welcome Day event will be held at the Lake Land College Effingham Technology Center on Thursday, August 27th from 10 am to 12 pm.

To learn more about Lake Land College Welcome Week 2026, visit the Lake Land College website at LakeLandCollege.edu/Current-Student/Welcome-Week-Technology-Skills/.

title: ISA ELECTIONS
full_story:
The Illinois Soybean Association (ISA) elected new leadership during its annual public meeting on July 29th in Champaign.

At the meeting, Bryan Severs was re-elected Chairman of ISA.  Severs is a third-generation farmer in Vermillion County, where his family raises corn, soybeans and cattle.  He has served as ISA’s District 7 Director since 2020 and previously took on additional leadership roles including Treasurer and Soybean Production Committee Chairman.  Severs also currently serves as Chairman of US Identity Preserved Alliance (USIPA) and as an American Soybean Association (ASA) Director.

Other elected executive committee members include Brady Holst of Plymouth, Vice Chairman; Rob Shaffer of El Paso, Treasurer; Scott Gaffner of Greenville, Secretary; and Emily Lovelady of Tamaroa, Assistant Treasurer-Secretary.

At the June 2026 Illinois Soybean Board meeting, Tim Scates was elected District 16 Director representing Clay, Wayne, Richland, Edwards, Lawrence, Wabash and White counties; and Trent Maxwell was elected District 14 Director representing Cumberland, Clark, Effingham, Jasper and Crawford counties.

title: RESTORATION OF LINCOLN HERNDON OFFICES
full_story:
The Illinois Capital Development Board (CDB), in partnership with the Illinois Department of Natural Resources (IDNR), completed a full restoration of the historic Lincoln-Herndon Law Offices in downtown Springfield, improving accessibility and safety at the building.

The $3.9 million Rebuild Illinois capital investment focused on renovating key architectural elements to their original character.  The scope of work included repairing damaged wood, painting, removing and restoring historic finishes, replacing floors and windows, and demolishing parts of the building that were deteriorated.

Many infrastructure upgrades were completed, including adding new air conditioning units, ductwork, lighting, and closed-circuit television (CCTV).  Additionally, the project involved the abatement of asbestos-containing materials and upgrading security systems, fire alarm systems, and fire sprinkler components to ensure the safety of employees and visitors.

The Lincoln-Herndon Law Offices are within the only remaining building in which Abraham Lincoln maintained a law office.  The structure consists of the surviving portion of a three-story brick commercial block constructed in 1840-1841.  The exterior is in the Greek Revival architectural style.  Located on the Old State Capitol Plaza in downtown Springfield, the building is a state historic site operated by IDNR.

“The Lincoln-Herndon building, where Abraham Lincoln practiced law for nearly a decade before moving on to elected office and eventually the presidency, is one of the capital city’s historic architectural treasures,” said IDNR interim Director Renee Snow.  “We are excited about the completion of this restoration project and are eager to welcome visitors and the community back to this special site.”

“To preserve historic infrastructure across our state, we must make the necessary renovations and improvements to modernize the facilities,” said CDB Executive Director TJ Edwards.  “The Lincoln-Herndon Law Offices received the required accessibility and safety upgrades, and the building’s features were carefully restored to its original beauty.”

The Lincoln-Herndon Law Offices project is one of several investments in Springfield’s historic downtown area.  Nearby, significant improvements of the interior and exterior of the Old State Capitol State Historic Site, also operated by IDNR, are nearing completion.  The enhancements prevent any additional decline to the facilities, allowing future visitors to enjoy some of Illinois’ most treasured historic landmarks.
